title: The Drop of Geneva
premise: Ada Kavanagh has spent nine years laundering reputations, not money—scrubbing dirty wealth until it looks clean, working cases her employers want unattributed. When a man named Ilan Roth repays a debt she has no memory of incurring, she is pulled into a ledger of favors that predates her own reinvented identity, and learns the stranger's 'favor' was the erasure of who she used to be. The ledger's next entry is a payment scheduled for dawn: a staged industrial accident at Geneva's water treatment works, timed to a private extraction flight that will carry the true principals out of Europe forever. To stop it, Ada must recover the memories she paid to lose and decide whether the woman she was deserves to survive. In the end she stops the attack, lets the flight leave with a poisoned ledger aboard, and walks into Geneva's train station as no one at all—finally free, finally nameless.
about_author: Bram Marchetti is the pen name of a former compliance consultant who spent a decade inside the machinery of international finance before walking away. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to not exist.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She closes an unattributable case in Zurich, scrubbing a shipping magnate's fortune, then returns to her deliberately bland Geneva apartment. The beat is controlled numbness—competence as anesthesia, and the first hint she cannot remember choosing this life.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A stranger, Ilan Roth, intercepts her at a café and repays a debt from 'Prague, eleven years ago'—a favor she has no record of. He leaves a key and a warning. The beat is vertigo: her flawless memory has a hole shaped like a person.

chapters.title: Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The key opens a Geneva safe-deposit box containing a handwritten ledger of favors, names redacted except hers, with a final entry dated tomorrow: 'payment in full, dawn.' The beat is dread dressed as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: What the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilan's POV. He watches Ada's building, recalling the Prague operation that erased her identity—and the price he paid for his part in it. The beat is guilt; he came to settle accounts before the ledger's owner settles them first.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Nobody
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She audits her own past and finds it manufactured: no school records before a certain date, a landlord who remembers her arriving with nothing. The beat is quiet terror—the self she defended was a product she delivered to herself.

chapters.title: The Collector
chapters.summary: Antagonist's POV (unnamed, 'the Auditor'). Introduced mid-calculation, reviewing the ledger and marking Ada's file 'recoverable asset.' The beat is chilling administrative menace—evil as portfolio management.

chapters.title: Prague, Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Fragmented flashback, Ada's POV. Sensory shards: a hospital corridor, a woman's voice, the smell of the Vltava, her own signature on a consent form she can't read. The beat is drowning—memory returning against her will.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She confronts Ilan; he admits the 'favor' was buying her erasure from a purge of witnesses to a laundering network she once helped expose. The final ledger entry is the network's exit: an attack staged as an industrial accident, then a dawn flight from Cointrin. The beat is betrayal and reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Flight Manifest
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Using financial-crimes tradecraft, she traces the charter jet's ownership through four shells to a Geneva private bank. The beat is the thrill of her old competence turned toward her own survival.

chapters.title: Someone Is Already Here
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her apartment has been searched; the ledger is gone; a message remains: 'You were paid once. Don't invoice twice.' The beat is violation—the past breaking into the present.

chapters.title: The Auditor's Offer
chapters.summary: The Auditor's POV. He meets Ada openly, offering her old life back—full memory, full identity—in exchange for standing down. The beat is temptation: the chance to know who she was, priced against everyone the dawn attack will kill.

chapters.title: Waterworks
chapters.summary: Ada and Ilan's POV, alternating. They case the water treatment plant and find the sabotage is elegant: a pressure failure timed to look like aging infrastructure, killing thousands softly. The beat is horror at how clean evil can be.

chapters.title: The Woman in Prague
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, fuller recovery. Ada remembers: she was a journalist whose exposé triggered the purge; the 'favor' Ilan repaid was saving her from its cleanup crew—at the cost of her name and her evidence. The beat is grief for a braver self.

chapters.title: Dead Drop on the Pont de la Machine
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A meet with a sympathetic bank insider goes wrong; Ilan takes a bullet covering her escape. The beat is the price of survival made literal—someone pays for her again, and this time she watches.

chapters.title: Interest Compounding
chapters.summary: The Auditor's POV. He accelerates the timeline after the failed meet, moving the flight to first light. The beat is tightening vise—Ada now has hours, not days.

chapters.title: The Consent Form
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She finds the original Prague consent form in the bank's archive: her own signature, and a clause she never read—her erasure was conditional, revocable, and she signed away the right to revoke. The beat is rage at the self who chose safety.

chapters.title: Everything Owed
chapters.summary: Ilan's hospital POV. Dying, he gives Ada the one thing the Auditor wants: the ledger's master copy, and the name of the flight's true principal—a man Ada's exposé nearly convicted. The beat is absolution; Ilan settles his account with his last breath.

chapters.title: Hours Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She chooses: she tips the plant's security anonymously, forcing the saboteurs to abort or improvise, and heads for Cointrin to confront the principal on the tarmac. The beat is resolve—no longer hiding, spending herself deliberately.

chapters.title: The Extraction
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax part one. On the airfield she trades the master ledger for the saboteur's abort code, broadcasting the plant's reprieve as the jet's engines spool. The beat is the high-wire moment—her memory and the city's lives in the same hand.

chapters.title: Payment in Full
chapters.summary: Climax part two, Ada's POV. The Auditor boards the flight; Ada lets it leave, knowing the poisoned ledger will unravel the network from inside within the week. He understands, and for one moment they recognize each other as the same kind of survivor. The beat is cold triumph.

chapters.title: What She Signed Away
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the aftermath, she reads her recovered Prague file and chooses not to reclaim her old name—the journalist died so someone could live; Ada honors both. The beat is mourning and integration: memory without reoccupation.

chapters.title: No One at All
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Weeks later, she walks into Geneva's main station with one bag and no ledger, taking a train with no destination chosen. The beat is earned freedom—survival's price finally paid in full, and worth it.
